rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING CERTAIN BENEFITS AND INCENTIVES TO SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICS TEACHERS
rows.abstract: \"Science and Mathematics Teachers Development.\" The bill provides measures that will attract bright students in mathematics and science to pursue a career in science teaching, enable them to advance in their specialization, sustain their interest in the field, and encourage them to stay on teaching science.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM THE AMUSEMENT TAX AS PROVIDED UNDER PARAGRAPH THREE OF SECTION ONE HUNDRED TWENTY-THREE OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AS AMENDED, BOXING CONTESTS FOR A RECOGNIZED WORLD TITLE
rows.abstract: The bill exempts from amusement tax the holding of boxing contests for a recognized title.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-07-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE NORTHERN SAMAR PROVINCIAL HOSPITAL IN CATARMAN, NORTHERN SAMAR, INTO EASTERN VISAYAS REGIONAL HOSPITAL UNDER THE SUPERVISION, CONTROL AND MANAGEMENT OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

rows.status: Approved by the House on 2006-11-14, transmitted to on 2006-11-22 and received by the Senate on 2006-11-22

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF A HOME FOR THE AGED AND DISABLED IN EVERY CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICT OF THE PHILLIPINES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The bill authorizes the Home for the Aged and Disabled to provide consultative services, including diagnosis, cure and prevention of diseases of the aged and disabled; rehabilitation hall with facilities for physiotheraphy and gymnasium for physical rehabilitation; a nutrition clinic; and a research ward on the care and treatment of aged and disabled patients. The requirements for admission to the home are: a) at least 62 years of age; b)in the case of the disabled, regardless of age, cannot move freely; c) of good moral character; and d) without any visible means of support.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 5(a) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3779, ENTITLED 'AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE REGULATION OF THE ORGANIZATION AND OPERATIONS OF SAVINGS AND LOAN ASSOCIATIONS' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill directs loans and savings associations to grant loans to qualified borrowers of an amount not exceeding Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00) or the amount deposited by the borrower plus his four (4) month's salary or regular income whichever is higher.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE USE OF PLASTIC BAGS, STYROFOAM, ALUMINUM FOILS AND NONBIODEGRADABLE MATERIALS, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill prohibits the use of plastic bag, Styrofoam, aluminum foils and non-biodegradable materials as packaging materials of goods sold by sari-sari stores, groceries, market vendors, sidewalk vendors, hawkers, department stores and similar establishments.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-02-01

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-02-01

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING HAZARD PAY TO ALL DULY APPOINTED MEMBERS OF BARANGAY TANOD BRIGADES DURING THEIR INCUMBENCY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill grants all duly appointed members of the barangay tanod brigades a hazard pay, during their incumbency, in the amount of Two Hundred Pesos (P200.00) per month.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEDUCTING THE COST OF DEVOLVED FUNCTIONS AND PERSONNEL FROM THE SHARE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS IN THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT AND THE TOTAL COST SO DEDUCTED SHALL BE DISTRIBUTED AND REMITTED DIRECTLY TO THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS CONCERNED AND REVISING THE FORMULA FOR ALLOCATING FUNDS TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO CORRECT INEQUITIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 285 OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill provides that AFTER DEDUCTING THE COST OF THE DEVOLVED FUNCTIONS AND PERSONNEL, AND THE COST OF THE CITY-FUNDED HOSPITALS, EXCLUDING CAPITAL OUTLAYS, THE TOTAL COST SO DEDUCTED SHALL BE DISTRIBUTED AND REMITTED DIRECTLY TO THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS CONCERNED AND THE NET OR BALANCE OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT SHALL BE ALLOCATED in the following manner: (a) Provinces - 23%; (b) Cities - 23%; (c) Municipalities - 34%; (d) Barangays - 20%: Provided, however, that the share of each province, city and municipality shall be determined on the basis of the following formula: (a) Population - 55%; (b) Land area - 20%; (c) Equal sharing - 25%.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT LIMITING THE HOURS OF OPERATION OF NIGHTCLUBS, COCKTAIL LOUNGES, BARS AND SIMILAR ESTABLISHMENTS, AND PENALIZING THE VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: The bill prohibits nightclubs, cocktail lounges, bars or similar establishments serving liquor, wint or intoxicating drink, from opening for business earlier that 5:00 p.m. and later than 1:00 a.m.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GAMES AND AMUSEMENTS since 2004-07-28

rows.mother_status: Printed copies distributed to members on 2007-01-24
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING EQUAL RIGHT TO WIVES AND HUSBAND, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 333, 334 AND 344 OF ACT NUMBERED 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: The bill substitutes the terms \"adultery\" and \"concubinage\" under Articles 333 and 334 of the Revised Penal Code with the term \"infidelity\" in order to attune the Code to the fundamental equality of women and men before the law.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05729

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING TWENTY PERCENT  (20%) DISCOUNT ON THE PURCHASE OF CELLCARDS BY A SENIOR CITIZENS WHOSE INCOME IS NOT MORE THAN ONE HUNDRED TWENTY THOUSAND PESOS (P120,000.00) PER ANNUM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'LAW MAXIMIZING THE CONTRIBUTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS TO NATION BUILDING, GRANT BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES'
rows.abstract: This bill grants a twenty percent (20%) discount on the purchase of prepaid cellcards by a senior citizen whose income is not more than ONE HUNDRED TWENTY THOUSAND PESOS (P120,000.000.00) per annum, provided that the senior citizen shall purchase only one cellcard a month.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2004-07-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE AND FREE PORT IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF SAN JOSE AND IN THE MUNICIPALITIES OF BOBON AND CATARMAN, ALL IN THE PROVINCE OF NORTHERN SAMAR, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

rows.author: C062
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING SENIOR CITIZENS WHOSE INCOME IS NOT MORE THAN ONE HUNDRED TWENTY THOUSAND PESOS (PHP 120,000.00) PER ANNUM TWENTY PERCENT (20%) DISCOUNT ON ELECTRICITY, WATER AND TELEPHONE BILLS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 2 AND 4 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432, ENTITLED \"AN ACT MAXIMIZING THE CONTRIBUTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS TO NATION BUILDING, GRANT BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill grants senior citizens whose income is less than P120,000.00 per annum, 20% discount on their electricity, water and telephone bills, amending for the purpose Sections 2 and 4 of Republic Act No. 7432. Senior citizens are now in the twilight years of their lives and most of them, having retired from work, have no sufficient income to support their families, particularly at this time when prices of commodities have skyrocketed beyond the reach of minimum wage earners.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY FOR UNAUTHORIZED ALTERATION OF ELECTION RETURNS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Any member of the Board of Election Inspectors or Board of Canvassers who tampers, increases or decreases the votes received by a candidate in any election after the announcement of the results thereof in the polling place, unless so ordered by the Commission on Elections or a competent court, shall be criminally liable for serious election offense. If found guilty, the offender shall: (1) be punished with imprisonment of not less than six years and one day but not more than twelve years; (2) be disqualified to hold public office; and (3) be deprived of the right of suffrage.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C001
rows.mother_status: Approved on Third Reading on 2006-12-20
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE INTERNAL AFFAIRS SERVICE FOR THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE TITLE V OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGHTY-FIVE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-ONE ENTITLED, \"AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REFORM AND REORGANIZATION OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AS AMENDED\" APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Under this bill, the function of the Internal Affairs Office (IAO) TO SERVE AS AN INDEPENDENT, IMPARTIAL AND OBJECTIVE INSTITUTIONAL WATCHDOG AGENCY FOR THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE is underscored. The bill contains provisions on: qualification requirements for the IAO Head; organization, appointments, entry qualification, promotions, career development and incentives, records management and disciplinary decisions.
rows.status: Substituted by HJR0019

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY TO ANY GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEE WHO HAS RENDERED AT LEAST TEN (10) YEARS CONTINUOUS GOVERNMENT SEVICE WITHOUT TAKING ANY CIVIL SERVICE EXAMINATION
rows.abstract: The bill confers government employees who have rendered continuous satisfactory service for at least ten (10) years with sub-professional or professional civil service eligibility, as the case may be, and qualifies them for appointment to any position under the following classifications: (1) Sub-professional Civil Service Eligibility: (a) Has rendered at least ten years continuous and satisfactory service; and (b) Has completed at least two years of college education leading to a college degree. Completion of at least 72 units in college or completion to a 2-year technical course with basic collegiate subjects, such as English and Mathematics, shall be considered equivalent to 2-year college education; (2) Professional Civil Service Eligibility: (a) Has rendered at least ten years continuous and satisfactory service; (b) Has completed a 4-year college education leading to a college leading to a college degree; and (c) A second grade or sub-professional civil service eligible.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PUBLIC DISPLAY OF PERSONS ARRESTED, ACCUSED, OR UNDER CUSTODIAL INVESTIGATION IN A DEGRADING MANNER, AND AMENDING FOR SUCH PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7438, ENTITLED \"AN ACT DEFINING CERTAIN RIGHTS OF PERSONS ARRESTED, DETAINED OR UNDER CUSTODIAL INVESTIGATION AS WELL AS THE DUTIES OF THE ARRESTING, DETAINING, AND INVESTIGATING OFFICERS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: The bill declares that NO PERSON ARRESTED, DETAINED OR UNDER CUSTODIAL INVESTIGATION SHALL BE PUT ON PUBLIC DISPLAY IN HAND CUFFS, WITH NAME TAGS OR OTHER TAGS, OR IN ANY MANNER CAUSING OR TENDING TO CAUSE DEGRADATION, HUMILIATION, DISHONOR, DISCREDIT, RIDICULE OR CONTEMPT, NOR SHALL SUCH PERSON BE PRESENTED TO THE PRESS IN SUCH MANNER. SUBJECT TO THE PRECEDING RESTRICTIONS, THE PUBLIC DISPLAY OR PRESENTATION TO THE PRESS OF ANY PERSON ARRESTED, ACCUSED, DETAINED, OR UNDER CUSTODIAL INVESTIGATION SHALL ONLY BE ALLOWED IF SUCH PERSON IS ASSISTED BY COUNSEL OF HIS CHOICE DURING THE PUBLIC DISPLAY OR PRESENTATION.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06046

rows.author: D067
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING A TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT (25%) DUSCOUNT ON TRANSPORTATION FARE FOR THE OFFICIALS OF THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN
rows.abstract: The bill explains that in the local level, the youth rely on their elected Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) officials to represent their interests, particularly in the local sanggunians. Young as they are, the SKs perform their tasks with unwavering idealism, vigor and dedication. The other reality, however, is that most SKs are also students and unemployed. The honoraria and other allowances that they receive from the local governments are barely adequate to support the various programs and activities they they undertake.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2005-02-14

rows.author: D067
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF TECHNICAL-INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SCHOOLS IN ALL THE REGIONS OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND APPRORPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The bill provides high school graduates with a better and affordable option in the matter of technical education. With the establishment of technical and information technology schools in all regions in the country that offer free and affordable technological education, the country will be ensured of a continuous generation of highly-trained graduates who are at par with the best in the world.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2005-08-15

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE TEACHING OF ECOLOGY IN ALL ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY LEVELS, WHETHER PUBLIC OR PRIVATE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The inclusion of ecology in the curriculum of elementary and secondary levels aims to inculcate in the youth ecological awareness and vigilance and make them understand more the dynamic relationships which support and maintain the bio-system.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D067
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL BAMBOO AND RATTAN DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Integrated National Bamboo and Rattan Development Program
rows.abstract: \"Integrated National Bamboo and Rattan Development Program.\" The Program shall cover the following: (1) Propagation or production of high quality, genetically superior planting stocks through sexual and macro and micro-sexual means; (2) Dispersal or distribution of planting materials at a nominal amount; (3) Production or bamboo farming and/or plantation development and management; (4) Utilization, processing and marketing including high value product development; (5) Training and extension, including technology packaging and transfer; and (6) Research and technology.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-11-21

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE THE AUTHORITY TO SETTLE MINOR CRIMINAL OFFENSES
rows.abstract: This bill authorizes to the Department of Justice (DOJ) through the Office of the Chief State Prosecutor, to bring together to an extra-judicial settlement the parties to a criminal action involving minor offenses. Minor offenses are offenses punishable by imprisonment not exceeding one (1) year and/or a fine not exceeding Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D067
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO HELP INSURE THE SAFETY OF BANK DEPOSITS AND FUNDS THEREBY STRENGTHENING THE OPERATIONS OF BANKING INSTITUTIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill helps in ensuring the safety of bank deposits and funds thereby strengthening the operations of banking institutions. It authorizes all banking institutions recognized and accredited by the Banko Sentral ng Pilipinas to provide special security services of their banking activities and operations and to procure and possess firearms for security purposes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D067
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO PROVIDE AT LEAST ONE (1) DENTIST IN EVERY MUNICIPALITY OF EVERY PROVINCE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The bill aims to provide one (1) dentist in every municipality of every province under the control and supervision of the Department of Health. Directs the Department of Health to issue rules and regulations for the effective implementation of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D067
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING SUBSIDY TO PRIVATE HOSPITALS AND CLINICS WHICH ADMIT FOR CONFINEMENT AND TREATMENT INDIGENT PATIENTS UNDER EMERGENCY CASES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill grants subsidy from the government for the hospital expenses of indigent patients admitted and confined in private hospitals and clinics under emergency cases.  It further requires all persons who wish to avail of the financial assistance granted under this Act to apply for an indigent identification card with the Department of Social Welfare and Development. Directs hospitals concerned to transmit monthly billings to the Department of Health of the total emergency admission fees extended to emergency patients.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D067
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 63, TITLE II OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill amends the present laws on marriage to allow the innocent spouse, who has been granted a decree of legal separation, to initiate the necessary petition before the proper courts to finally terminate their marriage and to re-marry, after a lapse of five (5) years from the date of issuance of the decree. Requires the petitioner during the hearing to properly establish the following elements: (1) That the petitioner is the innocent spouse; (2) That five  years have elapsed from the time the decree of legal separation became final and executory; and (3) Reconciliation between the spouses is no longer possible.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D067
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE DESIGNATION OF AT LEAST ONE TOURISM OFFICER IN EVERY MUNICIPALITY AND CITY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill aims to provide one (1) Tourism Officer in every municipality and city who would promote the economic, social and cultural development of their respective areas through income generating tourism promotions and development programs and projects. Prioritizes municipalities or cities where tourism is considered a major local industry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.abstract: Rationale: The Congressional Representative, as distinguished from those from the party0list, represents a definite political subdivision, a District. He is a local leader, inasmuch as he represents the interests of his constituents in the halls of Congress and before departments and agencies the government. However, he is also a national stakeholder and in performing his duties, he is not limited to promoting only parochial concerns but also issues and causes that affect other localities or the entire country as well. With all these concerns on his burden, it is not suprising that the Congressman is, perhaps, the most visited public official, especially when he is in his district, thus this bill.

rows.title_short: Gifted Children and Science-Oriented Youth Act
rows.abstract: \"Gifted Children and Science-Oriented Youth Act.\" This bill states the following objectives: (1) Identify the gifted Filipino children and science-oriented youth at the earliest age possible; (2) Establish a Center for the identification and nurturance of Filipino gifted children and science-oritented youth; (3) Provide scholarship grants and other forms of assistance for identified Filipino gifted children and science-oriented youth; (4) Provide funds for research and development, curriculum development, training of parents, teachers and other personnel; (5) Provide incentives to government institutions and the private sector that will participate in the implementation of this Act; and (6) Establish and maintain linkages with national and international institutions involved in programs on giftedness.
